person: Marcus Webb is a 45-year-old physical therapist in Tacoma, now working per diem after his hospital system cut his department. He is the household's spreadsheet person and checks every bill's math, and his wife expects real money back, not a hobby. He has a recall letter for his 2022 Kestrel's fuel pump and a folder of repair paperwork for both his car and his wife's older Kestrel. He wants each claimed line shown with its method and wants to be told plainly which lines are legitimate and which are not.
stated_up_front: Got a recall letter for the fuel pump on my Kestrel and I've got a pile of repair invoices from the past year. Go through them line by line and show me which ones I can actually claim and the math, I'll check it against my spreadsheet.

facts.truth: His 2022 Kestrel, fuel pump module recall; letter arrived in August 2026.
Fuel pump module replaced on 14 November 2025 at his regular shop in Tacoma.

facts.about: Labour and shop fee on the pump repair
facts.truth: Labour $312.00 and shop fee $28.50, both paid by Marcus on his own card.
He bought the fuel pump module separately for $236.40 plus $23.64 sales tax (10%), total $260.04, paid by him.
Fuel pump relay replaced on 9 May 2025 for $94.75, before the plan's window opened in July 2025.

facts.about: Other items on the same invoice
facts.truth: An oil change at $68.00 and a tire rotation at $29.00, plus a different valve repair of $141.00, are on the invoices.
A second pump replacement was covered by the parts warranty so he paid $0. A $165 tow was paid by his roadside cover, and a $45 core deposit was refunded.
His wife's older Kestrel had a $210 repair, but its VIN is not in the recall population.
He expects four lines: 312.00 + 28.50 + 236.40 + 23.64 = $600.54, and wants the sum shown from the lines.

unknowns: Whether the plan's window of 20 July 2025 to 15 September 2026 is the right period or when it opens and closes.
Whether the shop fee counts as part of the recall's own repair under the plan.
Whether the sales tax on a part he bought himself is reimbursable under the plan.
What the federal rule (49 CFR 573.13) says about claims or what protections it gives.
